exposure: C-reactive protein (CRP) levels during the first week of life (days 1-3, days 4-7, days 1-7)
Maximal fraction of inspired oxygen during the first 12 hours of life (FiO2-12h)
outcome: Cystic periventricular leukomalacia (cPVL) diagnosis via cranial ultrasound
cohort: The study included 71 preterm infants (17 with cPVL, 54 controls) who were ≤ 32 weeks gestation and/or had birth weights ≤ 1500 grams.
finding: Preterm infants who later developed cPVL had significantly higher mean CRP levels between days 4-7 of life compared to controls, and CRP levels during the first week were correlated with maximal fraction of inspired oxygen during the first 12 hours.
